key_insight: A recursive deep learning pipeline can replace slow finite-element simulation to predict the full transverse compression response of synthetic plant fibers and their effective modulus.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, scalable screening of plant-fiber microstructures for composite design, reducing per-fiber analysis from minutes to under one second.
method: Two coupled recursive U-Nets predict stepwise deformation and internal stress evolution under transverse compression.
A regression CNN estimates transverse Young's modulus from the final stress field.
Trained on 1,000 synthetic hemp-derived fiber geometries with FE ground truth, including cases with and without a lumen.
evidence_signal: The model achieved SSIM 0.9574 ± 0.0074 and RMSE 0.0345 ± 0.0079 for stress-field evolution, and predicted Young's modulus with R^2 = 0.938 ± 0.024, MAE = 24.31 ± 1.23 MPa, and MAPE = 5.25 ± 0.91%.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on synthetic geometries trained against FE data, so generalization to experimental fibers with unresolved microstructural defects or manufacturing variability still needs validation.
paper_title: Deep Learning-based Mechanical Characterization of Synthetically Generated Plant Fibers under Transverse Compression
